page: Amazon Web Services is4gen.8xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture and the ARMv8 64-bit AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor. The configuration provides 32 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with one thread per core, backed by 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster. System memory totals 192.0 GB RAM, establishing a 1:6 vCPU-to-memory ratio (6.0 GB RAM per vCPU). The server includes 30,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 50 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth without discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate reliable multi-core throughput alongside modest single-thread capabilities. The instance attained a PassMark CPU score of 17,399.65, a multi-core Geekbench score of 11,813.0, and 48,576.33 in stress-ng multi-core testing, all landing within median tiers. Conversely, single-threaded execution measures in lower bands, showing 971.0 in Geekbench single-core, 1,519.69 in single-core stress-ng, and 20.34 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. The ARMv8 architecture lacks x86-specific vector suites such as AVX-512, AMX, or SHA extensions, but retains standard AES cryptographic acceleration.

Data handling and memory throughput align well with intermediate data pipelines, showing 170.35 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth, 78.16 GB/sec write bandwidth, and 36.84 million operations/sec on Redis SET benchmarks. The 30,000 GB NVMe SSD volume combined with a high memory footprint provides substantial density for I/O-intensive workloads, trading raw per-core CPU performance for high local data storage capacity and network line rate. The profile is suited for distributed filesystems, high-volume database engines, stream ingestion, and search indexes.
description: Amazon Web Services is4gen.8xlarge is a storage-optimized ARMv8 instance powered by a 32-core AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, paired with 192.0 GB of RAM. Operating under the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers a 1:6 vCPU-to-memory ratio, 50 Gbps baseline network throughput, and 30,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, without attached GPUs. Benchmark profiles reveal moderate multi-core throughput, recording 11,813.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 48,576.33 in multi-core stress-ng, alongside mid-tier memory bandwidth of 170.35 GB/sec for uncached reads. Single-thread and decompression performance sit in the lower percentiles due to lower per-core clocks and standard instruction sets without AVX. The vast local NVMe capacity and 50 Gbps networking make this configuration well matched for high-throughput databases, search clustering, distributed filesystems, and large-scale data ingestion pipelines.
